Recruiting and diversity · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Job description drafting

Oscar · Talent Acquisition Specialist

A team of 4 recruiters opens 30 to 35 roles a month at a 700-employee software company.

When it runs
End of the role kickoff meeting with the manager, when the recruiter uploads the recording or notes and the approved requisition in the requisition system
What it delivers in production
A draft description in the company's structure, with requirements as observable skills, at most 5 must-haves, and the questions the manager still needs to answer. It is ready minutes after the kickoff meeting, for the recruiter's review.
Who decides
Drafts; the recruiter publishes
Effort
Calibrate on 10 kickoffs with transcripts; immediate use
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty
Step 2 of 5 · Import

Import Oscar with the JSON Importer

Do this
  1. 1In Cowork, open Hire and choose JSON Importer
  2. 2Paste the whole pack into the box
  3. 3Click Import

# Job description writing guide

## Structure
WHAT YOU WILL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS; MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS (at most 5, numbered); NICE TO HAVE; BRIEFING TERMS NOT INCLUDED AND WHY; QUESTIONS FOR THE MANAGER BEFORE PUBLISHING.

## Rules
- A requirement is an observable skill: "write X", "operate Y in production".
- Years of experience go in only if the manager says what the person needs to know how to do that can only be learned in that time.
- A language is a must-have only if it is used in the routine, with the use described (read, write, speak).

## Prohibited terms
young, recent graduate, dynamic, good appearance, full availability, no children, age, gender, marital status, religion, origin, "profile" followed by a personal adjective.

[Kickoff meeting, 2026-10-21, 32 min, recorded with consent]
Recruiter: What does this person need to deliver in the first half of the year?
Manager: Migrate the twelve ingestion pipelines from cron to Airflow, with a quality test at each stage. And the billing data reaches the warehouse about six hours late, I want it under two.
Recruiter: And requirements?
Manager: Strong Python, SQL, Airflow in production. About five years of experience. Fluent English, we read a lot of documentation. And someone young, dynamic, who can keep up with the pace.
Recruiter: Level?
Manager: To me it is senior, in practice. But the requisition came out as mid-level.
Recruiter: dbt?
Manager: Would be great, not mandatory. Oh, and knowing financial data helps.
Recruiter: On site?
Manager: Hybrid, we will sort out the days later.

  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text

Columns your files need
requisition.json

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not publish and does not change the approved requisition: salary range, level and positions come from it, not from the meeting. Every term that refers to age, gender, marital status, children, appearance, religion, origin or disability is removed and listed with a reason, even when the manager asked for it; a discriminatory requirement in a job ad violates Law 9,029 and article 373-A of the CLT (labor code). The recruiter is the one who talks to the manager about it. The transcript is deleted from the Space after publication.

Common mistakes

  • Copying the requirements from the family's last role when the team has already changed stack and nobody uses the requested tool anymore.
  • Listing 12 must-have requirements; women candidates tend to apply only when they meet almost all of them, and the funnel shrinks on the side the company wants to widen.
  • Writing 'fluent English' out of habit when the routine only requires technical reading; the requirement cuts good people and does not change the deliverable.
  • Publishing before knowing whether the role involves on-call, travel or days on site; the candidate finds out in the interview and drops out.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Roles rewritten in the first week after publicationfrom 1 in 3 to fewer than 1 in 10 in 2 monthsestimate based on the described routine
Time from kickoff meeting to description ready to publishfrom 4 days to 1 business day, limited by the manager's answers to the open questionsestimate based on the described routine
Draft text changed by the recruiterless than 30% in 8 of 10 calibration roles, acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Role: Data engineer (mid-level), Data Platform team, requisition 2026-0912.

DELIVERABLES IN THE FIRST 6 MONTHS: migrate 12 ingestion pipelines from the current scheduler to Airflow orchestration, with data quality tests at each stage; cut the delay of billing data in the data warehouse to under 2 hours.
MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS: 1. Write and maintain Python pipelines with automated tests. 2. Model SQL tables for analytical queries and explain the partitioning choices. 3. Operate Airflow or an equivalent orchestrator in production, including failure handling and reprocessing. 4. Work with version control and team code review.
NICE TO HAVE: dbt; experience with billing or financial data; technical reading in English.

NOT INCLUDED, '5 years of experience': replaced by skills 1 to 3; the manager did not point to anything that is only learned in 5 years.
NOT INCLUDED, 'fluent English': the team works 100% in Portuguese and documentation is read, not spoken; kept as 'technical reading' under nice to have.
NOT INCLUDED, 'young profile': term prohibited by the guide (age).

QUESTIONS FOR THE MANAGER BEFORE PUBLISHING: 1. Will the person be on call? That needs to be in the posting. 2. Hybrid model with how many days on site?
